qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Tesco is the undisputed UK grocery market leader (~28% market share) with massive purchasing power, Clubcard loyalty ecosystem, and Booker wholesale network. However, it operates in a fiercely competitive UK grocery market where it lacks unconstrained pricing power >= inflation. To prevent market share leakage to hard discounters (Aldi, Lidl), Tesco is forced to match Aldi on 600-700+ core staple lines ('Aldi Price Match') and use Clubcard prices defensively. Full-cycle GAAP ROIC across the total invested capital base (including store leases) averages ~7.8%, falling well short of the 12% compounder hurdle.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC ~7.8% full-cycle vs 12% hurdle, REJECT). UK supermarket market leader constrained by perpetual price competition with Aldi/Lidl; forced into defensive Aldi Price Match on staple goods, resulting in wafer-thin operating margins (~4.0-4.3%) and sub-hurdle full-cycle capital returns.
qualitative.evidence: While unadjusted accounting ROIC excluding leases appears higher over recent inflationary years, Tesco's multi-year full-cycle ROIC on total capital employed is ~7.8%. Retail operating margins hover around 4.1-4.3%. The business relies on heavy 'Save to Invest' cost reductions to offset wage and input inflation rather than exercising autonomous pricing power above inflation.
